title: The Effectiveness and Durability of Pretraining Data Filtering in Protein Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.26651v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Pretraining filtering is one of the most common safeguards for open-weight language models. Here we study its effectiveness, durability and scalability using the ESM-2 family of protein language models. We find that filtering viral proteins from the pretraining data meaningfully degrades masked language modelling, mutation effect prediction and long-range contact prediction on viral proteins, while largely preserving performance on non-viral proteins. These effects are concentrated among proteins from human-infecting viruses, and grow as we scale models from 8M to 3B parameters. As models increase in size, we find that stringent filtering becomes more effective. However, fine-tuning on sequences from the removed viral families restores the lost performance. Although the cost to recover performance increases with model scale, even for the largest models it costs about 80 USD of H100 time. This work establishes pretraining filter

translated_title: 蛋白质语言模型中预训练数据过滤的有效性与持久性
translated_abstract: 预训练数据过滤是开放权重语言模型最常见的安全保障措施之一。本研究以ESM-2系列蛋白质语言模型为例，研究了其有效性、持久性和可扩展性。我们发现，从预训练数据中过滤病毒蛋白质会显著降低模型在病毒蛋白质上的掩码语言建模、突变效应预测和长程接触预测能力，同时在很大程度上保持对非病毒蛋白质的性能。这些影响集中在感染人类的病毒的蛋白质上，并随着模型参数规模从800万扩展到30亿而增大。随着模型规模的增加，我们发现严格的过滤变得更加有效。然而，在来自被移除病毒家族的序列上进行微调可以恢复失去的性能。尽管恢复性能的成本随模型规模增加而上升，但即使对于最大的模型，其成本也仅需约80美元的H100计算时间。这项工作确立了预训练过滤器……
tldr: 该研究利用ESM-2蛋白质语言模型发现，预训练数据过滤能有效削弱模型对病毒蛋白（尤其是人类感染病毒）的能力且随模型规模增大而更有效，但这种防御可通过约80美元成本的低成本微调轻易被恢复，揭示了预训练过滤作为安全保障的局限性。
en_tdlr: This study using ESM-2 protein language models demonstrates that pretraining data filtering effectively degrades model capabilities on viral proteins and becomes more stringent-effective at larger scales, yet this safeguard can be easily bypassed through fine-tuning at a cost of only about 80 USD.
